gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-goth: Noto Sans Gothic reads wide and modern, with counters big as glass beads. Blockletter pushes a tall, pencil-drawn midsection that holds its line without pressing harder, while the body's round forms open like parentheses and keep the text moving.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-gran: Noto Sans Grantha has tall little letters, flattened like pen-nib bowls, so nothing snags on a closed-up shape. And Blockletter cuts its strokes like ribbon of constant width, a display voice that leaves the quiet, steady reading to the body.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-guja: Clean and modern, with curved strokes that stop before they turn inward. Blockletter handles the round-tipped, pen-drawn punch of a display line, and Noto Sans Gujarati handles the reading, its tall a, e and s opening wide.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-gunj: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi reads contemporary, its lowercase as tall as a thick crayon mark and its terminals cut back to leave a big gap. And Blockletter draws plain constant-width lines up top, which makes it the bolder voice while the body does the quiet work of reading.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-gurm: Tall-bellied and tubing-smooth up top, with tong-like terminals below. But Noto Sans Gurmukhi keeps its ascenders close to the x-height, so a long passage moves along briskly and cleanly under Blockletter's looping strokes.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-hanu: Blockletter draws its tall-bellied letters with a ballpoint's even stroke. And it earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of the height with open terminals underneath.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-hebr: Bent-copper-pipe strokes on top, a dominant midsection below that swallows the line's height. Wide gaps between curves and stems make it the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-hk: A monoline stroke runs from start to finish in Blockletter, its midsection tall like a squat brush-pen belly. But Noto Sans HK takes over where reading begins, with large lowercase forms and brush ends lifted away before each curve closes.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-impe: Blockletter has a rope-like consistency in every stem, bowl and tail, drawn with a tall brush-pen belly. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic opens its c like pincers and keeps capitals close.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-insc: No swelling where curves meet stems, just pencil-drawn lines that never press harder. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian is the strongest counterpart, with big open eyes on every e and a and a deep middle band.
